overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding executive sessions on February 18 and March 4, 2025 for topics outside the enumerated purposes; tax abatement discussions were permissible, and older meetings were declined as untimely.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board convened in executive session without a lawful purpose at 29 meetings from September 2023 to March 2025; most were more than 30 days before filing.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint was therefore not timely filed with respect to meetings that took place more than 30 days before it was filed, and we decline to review those meetings.

allegations.summary: Executive sessions on tax exemption and abatement applications under Purpose 7 at the February 18 and March 4, 2025 meetings were challenged.
Board cited Purpose 3 (litigation strategy) for a personnel discussion in executive session on February 18 and March 4, 2025, with no pending or threatened litigation.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by convening in executive session on February 18 and March 4 to discuss such matters.

allegations.summary: Board discussed an Open Meeting Law complaint in executive session on February 18 and March 4, 2025, though no complaint against Board members had been filed then.
allegations.key_passage: Where that complaint was not a complaint brought against the members of the Board, it was not appropriate for the Board to discuss it in executive session, and in so doing the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements; a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Law’s requirements and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
